topic: How do LEO and MEO satellite constellations balance link budget margins against atmospheric attenuation in Ka/V/Q bands for sparsely populated regions?
response: LEO and MEO satellite constellations balance link budget margins against atmospheric attenuation in Ka/V/Q bands by employing adaptive coding and modulation, data rate adaptation, and onboard adaptive power allocation to mitigate impairments. Site diversity and link power control are also used to compensate for increased atmospheric effects at higher frequencies.
reference_context: The context highlights the importance of mitigating atmospheric impairments, particularly in Q/V band frequencies (40-50 GHz), which is expected to be used by large gateways in future satellite communications systems. Techniques such as link power control, site diversity, and adaptive coding and modulation are mentioned as methods to counteract these effects.
